name: What If a Garage Addition Finds Foundation or Drainage Problems?

mainEntity.name: What happens if a garage addition reveals foundation or drainage problems in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What happens if a garage addition reveals foundation or drainage problems in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden foundation and drainage problems are common reasons garage addition budgets increase after work starts. If the soil is unstable, the slab area is uneven, or water flows toward the structure, the contractor may need to add grading, drainage improvements, deeper footings, or retaining details. In some cases, the original design cannot proceed safely until the issue is corrected. This is why a site visit and careful preconstruction evaluation matter so much in Los Angeles County, where lots can vary widely. Homeowners should ask contractors how they handle unforeseen conditions and whether the contract includes an allowance for site surprises. A clear change-order process is important because these issues can affect both cost and schedule. The best contractors explain the risk early instead of pretending every lot will behave the same way.
acceptedAnswer.description: If hidden foundation or drainage problems are found, the contractor may need to redesign part of the project, add engineering, or perform extra site work before construction continues. These issues often lead to change orders and schedule adjustments.
